You are auditing part of a Kanban board for "Kodely" — a planned AI website/app builder (a rocket.new/Lovable/Bolt competitor) whose moat is that sister company Nxeon owns the hosting infrastructure. You are doing a quality/completeness audit.

Read the full board dump at: /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/board-dump.txt

Focus ONLY on these columns: "Features & Table-Stakes", "Design & UX", "Builder / Editor UX", "AI / Codegen Engine". (Skim others for overlap context, but only audit these.)

Key context: the product core is a chat + live-preview editor that turns one plain-English sentence into a real, deployable app; non-developers are the target audience; reliability (green-build-first-try) and design quality (not "AI slop") are differentiators; it should reuse Nxeon patterns (auth, billing, streaming Build-with-AI UX). An opt-in "Cinematic" hero style exists (procedural WebGL default, paid Seedance premium).

Produce a CONCISE, structured report:
1. IMPROVE — specific existing cards that are weak/vague/redundant and exactly how to sharpen them (reference titles).
2. ADD — genuinely missing product/UX cards (title + one-line rationale). Real gaps only. Think about the full builder lifecycle: onboarding, the editor, generation UX, backend building, testing/QA of generated apps, publishing, post-launch editing, mobile/responsive, accessibility, i18n, collaboration, keyboard/perf, offline/error states.
3. ISSUES — duplicates, miscategorization, missing dependencies.
4. TOP 5 — the 5 highest-leverage items (improve or add), ranked.

Be specific and terse. Return only the report as text. No preamble.

334	COLUMN: Features & Table-Stakes  (44 cards)
335	============================================================
336	
337	[HIGH/FEATURE] 25+ one-click integrations catalog
338	Rocket ships **25+ built-in integrations**: Supabase, GitHub, Stripe, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Perplexity, Twilio, Notion, Figma, Mixpanel, Linear, Google, Resend, Mailchimp, and more. Kodely needs a comparable connector library (auth, DB, payments, email, LLM providers, analytics) to be credible at parity. Source: https://www.rocket.new/build
339	
340	[HIGH/FEATURE] One-click deploy, hosting, custom domain, SSL
341	Table stakes: Rocket offers a 'Launch' one-click staging→production deploy, a public URL, custom-domain support, and SSL included (deployed via Netlify). Kodely must match one-click deploy + custom domains + SSL — and can go further with first-party hosting rather than depending on Netlify. Source: https://www.rocket.new/build , https://docs.rocket.new/help/faq
342	
343	[HIGH/FEATURE] Dual editing: visual click-to-edit + chat
344	Rocket supports **Visual Edit** (click a UI element in the live preview and modify it without code, web-only) alongside **Chat** (natural-language build/iterate, web + mobile), plus an IDE/code view. Kodely needs both a conversational editor and a direct-manipulation visual editor to hit parity; the visual editor is a common expectation for non-technical users. Source: https://docs.rocket.new/help/faq
345	
346	[HIGH/FEATURE] Version history with per-change rollback
347	Rocket places a **rollback button below each code change** so users can restore earlier app states. Reliable version history/rollback is essential for AI builders where generations can break things — Kodely must ship snapshot + one-click revert per iteration. Source: https://docs.rocket.new/help/faq
348	
349	[HIGH/FEATURE] GitHub sync + full source-code export
350	Rocket offers two-way GitHub sync (Next.js TS) and full source-code download so 'the code belongs to you'. Code ownership/export is a decisive trust factor for developers evaluating AI builders. Kodely should offer GitHub export and repo sync — ideally without Rocket's Next.js-only / paid-only limitations. Source: https://docs.rocket.new/help/faq , https://www.rocket.new/build
351	
352	[URGENT/FEATURE] Auto backend: DB schema + auth + REST endpoints
353	From a prompt, Rocket generates a full backend on Supabase: PostgreSQL schema, authentication (email/password + Google/GitHub social, password reset, protected routes), row-level security, file storage, and REST endpoints. Full-stack (not just frontend) generation is now table stakes — Kodely must auto-provision DB + auth + APIs, not just UI. Source: https://docs.rocket.new/integrations/supabase
354	
355	[HIGH/FEATURE] Payments/Stripe wiring built in
356	Rocket wires up Stripe (subscriptions, checkout) against the Supabase backend without a separate backend sprint, enabling monetizable SaaS apps out of the box. A prompt-to-paid-SaaS path (Stripe + subscription/billing scaffolding) is expected functionality Kodely should match. Source: https://www.rocket.new/blog/connect-backend-database-rocket-supabase
357	
358	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Cross-platform mobile app generation (Flutter)
359	Rocket generates **Flutter** apps for iOS + Android from the same prompt flow, with APK download for Android testing. If Kodely wants to claim 'website + SaaS builder' parity for mobile, it needs a mobile-generation story — or must clearly scope to web and differentiate on hosting/SaaS depth. Source: https://www.rocket.new/blog/flutter-app-builder-ai
360	
361	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Team collaboration: shared workspaces + roles
362	Rocket provides shared workspaces/projects, role-based access (Admin, Editor, Viewer), **team credit pooling**, and unlimited members on all plans. Collaboration (multiple seats sharing one credit pool with no per-seat fee) is a competitive feature that removes a common cost barrier — Kodely's seat/collaboration model should account for this. Source: https://www.rocket.new/build , https://www.rocket.new/pricing
363	
364	[URGENT/FEATURE] Fair-metering: don't bill for the AI's own mistakes
365	The single biggest complaint about BOTH leaders is being charged (credits/tokens) when the AI breaks and re-fixes its own code. Kodely can win trust with transparent metering: don't charge for failed/auto-reverted generations, show a live cost estimate before running, and cap error-loop retries. This directly attacks Lovable's 'slot machine' and Bolt's 'burned 500K tokens, bug still there' reputations. Sources: https://www.zite.com/blog/lovable-reviews , https://www.yeasitech.com/bolt-new-problems-solutions
366	
367	[HIGH/FEATURE] Robust agent + error-fixing loop control
368	Both tools degrade on complex apps via debug loops (fix one thing, break another). Table-stakes: an agent that plans multi-step, reads logs/DB, and — crucially — detects when it's looping, stops, and asks rather than burning budget. Consider checkpoint/rollback per change and diff-scoped edits instead of full-file rewrites (Bolt's rewrite-whole-file behavior is a named token sink). Sources: https://www.testingcatalog.com/lovable-2-0-introduces-chat-mode-agent-alongside-multiplayer-support/ , https://superdesign.dev/blog/bolt-review
369	
370	[HIGH/FEATURE] Instant live in-browser preview
371	Bolt's WebContainers (browser-side Node.js) set the bar for instant preview + real backend execution + terminal, with no server round-trip. Kodely needs fast live preview; options are licensing/using WebContainers, forking open-source bolt.diy, or a server-side ephemeral container per project. This is the hardest-to-clone capability and a core UX expectation. Sources: https://bytes.dev/archives/329 , https://github.com/stackblitz-labs/bolt.diy
372	
373	[HIGH/FEATURE] Managed backend (zero-setup) + BYO option
374	Lovable Cloud (auto-provisioned managed Supabase: Postgres, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime with AI-generated schema/RLS) removed the biggest non-coder blocker. Kodely should offer a zero-config managed backend AND a 'connect your own Supabase/DB' path — but avoid Lovable Cloud's lock-in complaint (no dashboard access / no service keys). Given Nxeon already runs hosting, a self-hosted managed backend could be a cost edge. Source: https://supabase.com/blog/lovable-cloud-launch
375	
376	[HIGH/FEATURE] Full code export & ownership, GitHub two-way sync
377	Both leaders let users own 100% of code with no lock-in — Lovable via zip download and two-way GitHub/GitLab sync (edits flow both directions). This is now table-stakes for trust; Kodely must ship clean, standard, readable project output (React/Tailwind + config) plus one-click GitHub sync from day one. Source: https://lovable.dev/faq/code-export
378	
379	[HIGH/FEATURE] One-click deploy + free custom domains
380	Expected baseline: publish to a live URL in one click plus attach a custom domain with automatic SSL, and remove builder branding on paid plans (Bolt bundles custom domains + no-branding into every paid tier). Nxeon's existing hosting/VPS + DNS stack is a natural advantage to make Kodely deploy targets first-party rather than reselling Netlify/Vercel. Sources: https://www.nocode.mba/articles/bolt-pricing-2026 , https://lovable.dev/blog/lovable-2-0
381	
382	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Stripe / payments integration for real SaaS
383	Both let users add Stripe checkout via a prompt (Lovable wires it through Supabase Edge Functions with secret storage). For a 'SaaS builder' Kodely, prompt-driven Stripe (checkout, subscriptions, webhooks, customer portal) plus secure secret management is essential to reach the money-path apps users actually monetize. Source: https://docs.lovable.dev/integrations/supabase
384	
385	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Multi-mode editing: chat + visual + code
386	Lovable 2.0 offers Agent Mode (autonomous), Chat Mode (plan-only), a Visual Editor for click-to-edit UI changes that cost NO credits, and Dev Mode for direct code. The free visual-edit path is a smart credit-saver users love. Kodely should support all three altitudes and make small visual tweaks free/cheap so users aren't spending AI credits to nudge padding. Source: https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/lovable-launches-version-2-0-with-smarter-chat-agent-multiplayer-features-and-security-scan/
387	
388	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Real-time collaboration & Teams
389	Both offer multiplayer/teams: Lovable supports real-time editing for up to 20 collaborators with shared credit pools, SSO and centralized billing on Business; Bolt Teams is $30/member/mo with admin controls. For agencies/studios (a Nxeon audience), shared workspaces + pooled credits + centralized billing are expected. Sources: https://www.testingcatalog.com/lovable-2-0-introduces-chat-mode-agent-alongside-multiplayer-support/ , https://www.nocode.mba/articles/bolt-pricing-2026
390	
391	[HIGH/FEATURE] Security scan on publish
392	Lovable 2.0 ships a built-in Security Scan that checks Supabase-backed apps for vulnerabilities (e.g. missing/exposed RLS) at publish time — important because AI-generated apps frequently ship insecure data access. Given Nxeon's own pentest history, a publish-time security scan (RLS, exposed secrets, auth gaps) is both a differentiator and a liability shield for Kodely. Source: https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/lovable-launches-version-2-0-with-smarter-chat-agent-multiplayer-features-and-security-scan/
393	
394	[NORMAL/IDEA] Native mobile output (Expo-style)
395	Bolt exports to native iOS/Android via Expo from the same prompts, with instant QR-code device preview — a gap Lovable doesn't fill. A mobile-app path (React Native/Expo) would let Kodely cover use cases neither leader fully owns and broaden the 'SaaS + app builder' pitch. Source: https://expo.dev/ai/bolt , https://natively.dev/bolt-new-for-mobile-apps

A genuinely usable free tier — enough to ship one small real app — plus token/credit rollover on paid plans are proven growth levers Kodely should copy. 706	COLUMN: AI / Codegen Engine  (21 cards)
707	============================================================
708	
709	[URGENT/FEATURE] Build a flow-engineered agent loop: plan → generate → run → read errors → fix
710	Bolt.new's core insight is **flow engineering** (à la AlphaCodium): break app generation into smaller sequential steps rather than one monolithic generation, which works better across model capabilities ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). The loop is: produce a plan, write files, run the dev server/build, capture errors, feed them back, and iterate with fix/ignore options. Kodely should implement this explicit state-machine loop rather than a single prompt→dump — it's the difference between apps that boot and apps that don't. This is the single most important engine decision.
711	
712	[HIGH/FEATURE] Diff-based edits over full-file rewrites
713	Bolt applies changes as **diffs using speculative decoding**, changing only the parts that need updating — far fewer tokens and faster iterations than rewriting whole files, which matters at scale ([buildthisnow.com/blog/tools/extensions/claude-code-vs-bolt](https://www.buildthisnow.com/blog/tools/extensions/claude-code-vs-bolt), [latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). Lovable by contrast plans first and rewrites larger sections, and is measurably slower (~60s vs ~30s per generation). Kodely should default to targeted diff/patch edits (search-replace blocks or unified diffs the model emits) and reserve full-file writes for new files or large refactors. Directly cuts token cost and latency.
714	
715	[HIGH/FEATURE] Model choice: Claude Sonnet as default, escalate to Opus for planning
716	Bolt.new and much of the category run on Anthropic's Claude (Bolt built an >$8M ARR business essentially as a 'Claude wrapper') because Claude leads at agentic coding ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt), [mastra.ai/articles/best-llm-for-coding](https://mastra.ai/articles/best-llm-for-coding)). Kodely already has Nxeon's Anthropic-based 'Build-with-AI' integration to reuse. Recommend **Claude Sonnet (4.5-class) as the workhorse** for edits/codegen and **Opus for the initial plan/architecture step**, with the model abstracted behind a router so a cheaper model can handle trivial edits. NOTE from memory: the Nxeon chat agent is still blocked on a valid/funded Anthropic key — Kodely inherits that dependency, so resolve billing first.
717	
718	[HIGH/FEATURE] Instrument the sandbox to feed real errors back to the agent
719	Bolt instruments WebContainers at the **process, runtime, and build levels** so the agent receives 'the state of the application and the errors from Node.js or the browser console' and can auto-fix ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). This closed error loop is why its output actually runs. Kodely must capture build output, dev-server logs, uncaught runtime exceptions, and browser console errors from the sandbox and pipe them structured into the agent's next turn. Without this, the model is fixing blind. Build the error-capture channel as part of the sandbox from the start.
720	
721	[HIGH/FEATURE] Context management for growing codebases — retrieve, don't dump
722	Bolt maximizes context ('the entire state of the application') for accuracy, but that only scales while projects are small ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). Chroma's Context Rot study found *every* frontier model degrades as input grows — a 200K window can show serious accuracy loss by 50K tokens, and facts buried mid-context cost 30+ accuracy points ([cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026](https://cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026/)). Kodely needs a retrieval layer: send the full tree/manifest but only the *relevant* file bodies (via embeddings + recent-edit heuristics), and keep the most important context at the start/end of the prompt. Plan retrieval before projects get big.
723	
724	[HIGH/CHORE] Prompt caching — the single biggest cost lever
725	Prompt caching gives a ~90% discount on cached input tokens and is the largest cost reducer for repeated system prompts; in Claude Code/Cline sessions, re-sending conversation history is ~50–60% of token spend and tool descriptions alone add 10–15K tokens per request ([fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization](https://fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization/), [pinggy.io/blog/tools_to_reduce_ai_coding_agent_token_usage](https://pinggy.io/blog/tools_to_reduce_ai_coding_agent_token_usage/)). Kodely should structure prompts so the stable system prompt, tool definitions, and unchanging project context sit in cacheable prefixes with Anthropic cache breakpoints. This is low-effort, high-savings and should be wired in before launch, not retrofitted.
726	
727	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Context compaction / conversation summarization
728	Long build sessions bloat context; Claude's context-compaction can condense history server-side (one reported case collapsed 132K tokens to 2K) and 'isolating work across separate context windows' keeps tasks from contaminating each other ([fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization](https://fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization/), [cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026](https://cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026/)). Kodely should summarize resolved turns, trim stale tool output, and maintain a compact rolling project-state summary rather than replaying the whole chat each turn. Keeps long iterative sessions affordable and accurate.
729	
730	[HIGH/FEATURE] Tool-use design: give the agent fs, terminal, npm, and console tools
731	Bolt gives the model complete control of the filesystem, node server, package manager, terminal and browser console ([github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new](https://github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new)). Kodely should expose a tight, well-described tool set — write_file, apply_diff, read_file, run_command, install_package, read_logs, restart_dev_server — each mapped to sandbox operations. Keep tool descriptions lean (they're billed on every call) and prefer a few composable tools over many niche ones. Good tool ergonomics are what let the model self-correct instead of guessing.
732	
733	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Retrieval/index over the project (file tree + embeddings)
734	When an agent lacks retrieval it wastes tokens reading whole files to find a few lines — the third-biggest token sink after history and tools ([fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization](https://fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization/)). Vector DBs work but get expensive; a hybrid of efficient file storage + targeted embedding search often costs less ([pinggy.io/blog/tools_to_reduce_ai_coding_agent_token_usage](https://pinggy.io/blog/tools_to_reduce_ai_coding_agent_token_usage/)). Kodely should maintain a live project index (symbol map + embeddings, refreshed on edits) so the agent can grep/semantic-search to the exact files it needs. Reuse Nxeon's existing Postgres with pgvector rather than adding a new vector DB.
735	
736	[HIGH/FEATURE] System/prompt design + a structured artifact output format
737	Bolt's quality comes largely from a carefully engineered system prompt that constrains the model into its step-by-step flow and a structured 'artifact' format for emitting files/commands (public in the open-source repo) ([github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new](https://github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new)). Kodely should define a strict output schema — plan block, then file-write and shell-command actions the runner parses deterministically — so parsing never depends on fragile prose. Invest real effort in the system prompt (stack conventions, when to diff vs rewrite, security rules); it's the cheapest quality lever and it's cacheable.
738	
739	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Stream generation to the UI (files + reasoning live)
740	Modern builders stream file writes and reasoning as they happen so users see progress instead of a spinner; this is core to the bolt/Lovable UX ([github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new](https://github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new)). Kodely should stream the model's tokens, surface each file being created/edited in real time, and show the plan up front. Streaming also lets users interrupt/redirect early, saving tokens on wrong directions. Reuse the streaming plumbing from Nxeon's existing Build-with-AI/chat agent.
741	
742	[HIGH/CHORE] Token metering + credit system (don't repeat Bolt's flat-rate mistake)
743	Bolt launched at $9/mo flat 'Netflix-model' access and users burned through allocations in weeks, creating scaling tension with inference cost ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). Kodely must meter token/compute usage per user from day one, expose a credits balance, and price plans against real Anthropic + sandbox cost. Track cost per project/message so heavy users are identifiable. Tie this to Nxeon's existing billing. This is a business-survival item, not an optimization.
744	
745	[HIGH/FEATURE] Execution-based evals: pass@k + a regression harness
746	Real codegen quality is measured by *running* the output, not reading it — generate code, run it in a sandbox, check against tests, with pass@k as the headline metric; system-level evals also cover retrieval, prompt design, tool use and guardrails ([promptfoo.dev/docs/guides/evaluate-coding-agents](https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/guides/evaluate-coding-agents/), [futureagi.com/blog/evaluating-coding-agents-2026](https://futureagi.com/blog/evaluating-coding-agents-2026/)). Kodely should build an eval suite of representative prompts ('todo app with auth', 'Stripe checkout page') that generates, boots the app in a sandbox, and asserts it builds + core flows work — run on every prompt/model change to catch regressions before shipping to users. Prevents silent quality drops when tweaking prompts or swapping models.
747	
748	[URGENT/CHORE] Guardrails: prompt-injection, secrets, and code-injection scanners
749	Coding agents are attack surfaces — a Feb 2026 attack on the Cline IDE started with a malicious GitHub issue *title* containing injected instructions; defenses need input guardrails (screen prompts) and output guardrails (screen generated code) ([futureagi.com/blog/evaluating-coding-agents-2026](https://futureagi.com/blog/evaluating-coding-agents-2026/)). A SecretsScanner catches invented/leaked credentials and a CodeInjectionScanner flags eval/exec/shell-interpolation/template-injection in generated code. Because Kodely will read user repos, GitHub issues, and pasted content into the agent, it must sanitize untrusted input and scan every generated file before commit/deploy. Given the CRITICAL RCE already found in Nxeon's DB Studio (memory), treat agent guardrails as a launch gate with a security review.
750	
751	[NORMAL/IDEA] shadcn/ui component retrieval for consistent, attractive UI
752	A big reason Lovable/v0 output looks good is that they generate against **shadcn/ui**, whose components are editable source the model can retrieve and adapt rather than invent styling from scratch ([techsy.io/en/blog/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0](https://techsy.io/en/blog/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0/)). Kodely should ship a curated component/block library (shadcn + a few opinionated layout blocks) and give the agent a retrieval tool to pull the right component source into edits, so UI stays consistent and polished across a project. This also cuts tokens (the model composes known components instead of hand-writing markup). Bonus: encode Nxeon's own brand theme (navy+violet+cyan per memory) as a preset for on-brand builds.
753	
754	[NORMAL/IDEA] Model routing + graceful degradation / fallback
755	Kodely will depend on Anthropic availability, and memory notes the Nxeon chat agent already ships a failure banner + graceful-degrade pattern for exactly this. Kodely should route by task (cheap model for trivial edits, Sonnet for codegen, Opus for planning), fall back to a secondary model/provider on outages or rate limits, and surface a clear degraded-mode banner instead of failing silently. Retry with backoff on transient errors and cap retries to protect token spend. Reuse the Nxeon chat agent's degradation UX directly.
756	
757	[LOW/IDEA] Optional multi-agent decomposition (planner / coder / reviewer)
758	Research on LLM multi-agent code generation shows splitting roles (a planner, a coder, and a reviewer/tester) can improve reliability on complex builds by isolating concerns into separate context windows ([arxiv.org/pdf/2604.16321](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.16321), [cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026](https://cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026/)). Kodely could add a lightweight reviewer pass that runs the eval/build and critiques the coder's output before showing the user. Keep it optional/behind a flag — it multiplies token cost, so gate it to complex prompts or paid tiers. Start single-agent, add this only if evals show it moves quality.
759	
760	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Auto-SEO for generated sites
761	Every generated site ships with sensible meta tags, OpenGraph/Twitter images, a sitemap, and structured data. Users won't add these; making sites rank is a real value-add.
762	
763	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Accessibility + performance budget on output
764	Run a11y checks and a Lighthouse/perf budget on generated output, and auto-fix common failures. Quality bar that separates Kodely from slop-generators.
765	
766	[HIGH/CHORE] Prompt/guardrail library + eval harness
767	A versioned library of system prompts + guardrails and an execution-based eval harness so engine changes are regression-tested (green-build-first-try can't silently drop).
768	
769	[HIGH/FEATURE] Large-project context management
770	Diff-based edits, file targeting, and retrieval so the engine stays reliable as projects grow beyond a single file/context window. The scaling wall most builders hit.

937	Surface the agent's plan and each step as it streams (files created, packages installed, commands run) so long generations feel alive rather than a spinner. 940	When the generated app throws a runtime/build error, capture it from the sandbox console and offer a 'Fix it' button that feeds the stack trace back to the agent, which patches, validates, and retries until it builds. 943	Lovable splits an interactive Chat Mode (plan, debug, reason — no code changes) from Agent Mode (executes the build). 946	Provide desktop/tablet/mobile breakpoint toggles (and a rotate control) in the preview toolbar so users can verify their generated site is responsive. Pair with a prompt convention so 'make it mobile-friendly' reliably adjusts Tailwind breakpoints. This is table stakes users expect from v0/Lovable-class tools. Ref: https://www.nxcode.io/resources/news/v0-by-vercel-complete-guide-2026
947	
948	[NORMAL/IDEA] Make the builder UI itself usable on mobile/tablet
949	The builders themselves are desktop-first; the three-pane chat+code+preview layout collapses badly on small screens. Kodely should ship a mobile builder mode (stacked/tabbed chat ↔ preview, hide the code pane, larger touch targets) so users can prompt and preview from a phone — a genuine gap in the market. Ref: https://designrevision.com/blog/forge-vs-bolt-vs-lovable-vs-v0-comparison
950	
951	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Project dashboard: list, rename, duplicate, deploy status
952	A home dashboard listing all projects with thumbnails, last-edited, deploy/domain status, and quick actions (open, duplicate, delete, export to GitHub). Rocket.new/Bolt organize work per-project with export and one-click deploy; make deploy state (draft / published / custom domain) visible at a glance. Refs: https://www.rocket.new/ai-app-builder , https://github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new
953	
954	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Template gallery + community remix
955	Offer a starter template gallery (SaaS dashboard, landing page, marketplace, portal, storefront) and a 'remix this' flow so users fork an existing public project as a starting point. v0 leans on shadcn/Tailwind primitives; a curated, on-brand template set reduces the cold-start problem and showcases quality. Refs: https://www.bitcot.com/top-10-ui-components-you-can-create-with-v0-by-vercel/ , https://websiteprompts.ai/
956	
957	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Guided onboarding + prompt-quality coaching
958	First-time users write weak prompts and get weak results; whole cottage industries sell 'prompts for Lovable/Bolt'. Bake in an onboarding that suggests structure (goal, pages, style, data), offers example prompts, and can auto-expand a terse prompt into a fuller spec before building. This directly improves first-generation success and retention. Ref: https://www.idlen.io/blog/10-best-prompts-lovable-bolt-cursor/
959	
960	[LOW/IDEA] Design-import: Figma / screenshot → app
961	Rocket.new and v0 both import Figma files (and images) and convert them into live, editable layouts, removing manual design-to-code translation. A screenshot-to-UI path ('clone this look') is a strong acquisition hook. Consider this a fast-follow once core generation is solid. Refs: https://docs.rocket.new/getting-started/introduction , https://vercel.com/blog/announcing-v0-generative-ui
962	
963	[LOW/IDEA] Precision edits via slash-commands
964	Rocket.new's 'Precision Mode' exposes 100+ slash commands for targeted edits (e.g. add a route, wire an API, add auth) — deterministic shortcuts that avoid vague prompting and reduce token spend on common operations. A curated slash-command palette is a good power-user layer over the chat. Ref: https://docs.rocket.new/getting-started/introduction
965	
966	[NORMAL/IDEA] Branding direction for 'Kodely' — name, tone, look
967	Name reads as friendly/approachable ('code' + '-ly'), leaning consumer/indie-maker rather than enterprise. Tone: encouraging, plain-language, anti-jargon ('describe it, we build it'). Visual direction to explore: a distinct accent (avoid the ubiquitous violet/indigo of Lovable/v0) with a clean, confident, slightly playful feel; a rocket/spark-free mark to differentiate from rocket.new/Bolt. Because Kodely sits under the Nxeon umbrella, keep it visually adjacent to but distinct from the Nxeon navy+violet+cyan brand. Deliverable: logo, wordmark, color tokens, 1-line positioning.
968	
969	[HIGH/FEATURE] Three-tier prompt help: chips + wizard + auto-enhance
970	Attack the #1 beginner churn driver ('I didn't know what to describe') with help at three altitudes, all optional: (1) example chips + template gallery for speed, (2) a base-prompt WIZARD for the unsure, (3) auto-enhance for free-form typers. The raw prompt box stays the default hero; help is opt-in, never a gate. Improving first-build success is the strongest determinant of retention.
971	
972	[HIGH/FEATURE] Base-prompt wizard: category → questions → editable spec
973	3-4 skippable steps: (1) What are you building? (business site / SaaS / internal tool / store / booking / portfolio / directory / dashboard) — deterministically selects stack, template & guardrails; (2) a few tuned questions per type (needs login? payments? key pages?); (3) look & feel (theme / logo / colors / tone); (4) review the composed spec + estimated credit cost, edit, then Build. Produces an EDITABLE prompt (transparency) and doubles as the plan-before-you-spend step.
974	
975	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Brand/style step to kill the generic 'AI purple'
976	The wizard's look-and-feel step (pick a distinctive theme, upload logo + brand colors, set tone) attacks the well-documented 'every AI app looks the same violet' weakness and feeds design tokens into the system prompt so output stays on-brand. Kodely's demoable design-quality differentiator, surfaced at the very first step.
977	
978	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Auto-enhance: expand a rough prompt into a full spec
979	For users who just type 'a website for my bakery,' a cheap/fast model expands it into a structured spec (pages, features, data, style) BEFORE building — shown to the user to tweak, never done invisibly. Zero friction, big first-result quality jump. rocket.new and others ship a version of this.
980	
981	[NORMAL/IDEA] Never force the wizard — raw box stays the default
982	Power users hate gates; the hero stays a single big prompt box. The wizard is an obvious 'Not sure where to start? Guide me' path beside it. Keep it fast (3-4 quick, skippable questions) so speed-to-first-build is never sacrificed to a long survey.
983	
984	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Cinematic is an opt-in template, not the default look
985	Not all sites should look like this. Cinematic/motion is a STYLE the user chooses, not the house style. In the builder's 'look & feel' step, offer styles: Minimal · Editorial · Bold · Cinematic (motion). Most sites default to clean/fast/static — better for SEO, conversion and load. Picking 'Cinematic' wires the procedural WebGL hero by default; paying users can upgrade a project to a bespoke Seedance clip.
986	
987	Guardrails when Cinematic is on: warn about weight/SEO/LCP; ALWAYS ship a reduced-motion + mobile-light fallback; lazy-load the WebGL/frames; keep text content in real DOM (not baked into the video) so it stays crawlable and accessible. Sell it as a deliberate choice for launch pages / brand sites, not for content-heavy or commerce sites where speed wins.
988	
989	[HIGH/FEATURE] Kodely 'Luxe' marketing-site design system (the approved look)
990	The user-approved aesthetic for kodely.me — Apple/luxury minimal. Codified so it's reusable.
991	
992	TYPE: Geist (display + body, 400-800) + Geist Mono for eyebrows/labels/urls. Display huge: hero clamp(3.2rem,8.2vw,7.4rem), section clamp(2.4rem,5.6vw,4.6rem); tracking tight (-.04 to -.05em); weight 600. Body 17px, grey, line-height ~1.55. Mono uppercase eyebrows, .14em tracking. font-feature-settings ss01,cv01,cv11.
993	
994	COLOR: near-monochrome. Light — bg #fff, ink #0b0a0d, ink-2 #605b66, hairline lines rgba(11,10,13,.09). Dark — bg #08070A, ink #f6f3f7, luminous. Warm gradient (#F72570 -> #FF6B67 -> #FF9868 -> #A33DFF) is RARE punctuation only: wordmark, ONE hero word, primary CTA, key accents. Soft neutral tints (blush/sage/sand/lilac) for imagery stand-ins.
995	
996	LAYOUT: extreme whitespace (section padding clamp(110-190px)), max-width ~1080px, centered hero. ONE hero object = a real miniature site inside a browser frame (genuine type hierarchy + real product names/prices + soft editorial color), NOT skeleton blocks. Feature sections = alternating full-width statement + one tasteful visual, never a 6-card grid. Full light + dark via CSS token swap + toggle.
997	
998	MOTION: quiet, physics-eased cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1); few elements moving at once. Loader assembles the abstract mark (~1s). One pinned 'Describe it / Generate it / Launch it.' Smooth count-ups. IntersectionObserver reveals (opacity+translateY, staggered d1..d4). Subtle magnetic on primary CTA only. Full prefers-reduced-motion fallback.
999	
1000	LOGO: abstract mark from 5 geometric shapes (capsule + circle + two ribbons + diamond) in the warm gradient; lowercase 'kodely' wordmark, -.05em. Tagline 'AI websites, simplified.' Reference build: scratchpad/kodely.html.
1001	
1002	[NORMAL/IDEA] Kodely brand motion language + cheap-look anti-patterns
1003	Principles (keep every animation meaningful and calm):
1004	- Ink dominates; gradient is punctuation, never a fill-everything.
1005	- One hero object per page; huge type + few words; whitespace IS the luxury.
1006	- Motion must mean something (particles=ideas, assembly=generation) and stay slow/smooth.
1007	- Fast interactions 100-300ms; major transitions 500-1000ms; atmosphere 5-20s; spring/eased, never linear except continuous drift.
1008	
1009	Anti-patterns that read CHEAP (learned across iterations, do NOT do):
1010	- Animated/looping gradient text or borders (reads like a GIF) -> use STATIC gradients.
1011	- Flat skeleton/placeholder blocks as 'mockups' -> show ONE real, detailed UI instead.
1012	- Many simultaneous rAF animations competing for frames -> feels janky; keep few, throttle with a single rAF + requestAnimationFrame guard.
1013	- Crowded multi-section card grids -> generic; prefer big spaced statements.
1014	- Generic system Arial -> always embed a real face (Geist) as @font-face data URI (CSP blocks CDNs in artifacts).
1015	- Candy-saturated gradients everywhere -> desaturate, add scrims, let neutrals breathe.
1016

3823	COLUMN: Builder / Editor UX  (19 cards)
3824	============================================================
3825	
3826	[HIGH/FEATURE] Editor workspace: chat + live preview
3827	The core canvas — an AI chat/command rail beside a live, interactive preview of the running site. This IS the product; everything else orbits it. Fast, resizable, keyboard-friendly.
3828	
3829	[HIGH/FEATURE] Click-to-edit on the canvas
3830	Select any element in the preview and edit it directly (text, color, spacing, swap image) — by clicking or by telling the AI 'make this bigger'. The difference between a toy and a tool for non-devs.
3831	
3832	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Visual inspector / property panel
3833	A panel to tweak the selected element's typography, color, spacing, and layout without prompts — for users who want direct control. Writes back to the same code.
3834	
3835	[HIGH/FEATURE] Version history, checkpoints & rollback
3836	Every AI change and manual edit is a saved checkpoint; one-click restore to any prior state. Removes the fear of 'the AI broke my site' — a top competitor complaint.
3837	
3838	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Undo / redo across AI + manual edits
3839	A unified history stack so undo works the same whether the last change came from a prompt or a click. Table stakes users assume exists.
3840	
3841	[HIGH/FEATURE] Code view + inline editing + export
3842	Show the real generated code, let advanced users edit it inline, and export/download or push to GitHub. Backs the 'you own the code' ownership moat.
3843	
3844	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Responsive preview (device frames)
3845	Preview desktop / tablet / mobile and fix responsive issues per breakpoint. Generated sites must look right on phones or they're worthless.
3846	
3847	[LOW/FEATURE] Comments / annotations on the preview
3848	Pin comments to elements for feedback/review (client ↔ agency). A cheap retention + collaboration lever.
3849	
3850	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Multi-page & file management
3851	Create/manage multiple pages and assets in one project, with navigation wiring. Real sites aren't one page.
3852	
3853	[HIGH/FEATURE] Streaming generation UX (stop / regenerate / branch)
3854	Watch the build stream in, stop it, regenerate a section, or branch an alternative — reuse Nxeon's Build-with-AI streaming + graceful-degrade UX.
3855	
3856	[HIGH/FEATURE] Plan-before-spend mode
3857	Before a costly build, show the plan + a credit estimate for the user to approve/edit. The core anti-bill-shock lever, in the editor.
3858	
3859	[HIGH/FEATURE] Error-recovery UX (auto-fix loop, visible)
3860	When a build fails or errors, show the diagnosis and the AI's fix attempts inline instead of dumping a stack trace. Reliability people can see is reliability they trust.
3861	
3862	[HIGH/FEATURE] Visual database / schema editor
3863	Create tables, fields and relations visually (or by prompt) — 'add a bookings table'. The backend-depth wedge vs frontend-only builders.
3864	
3865	[HIGH/FEATURE] Auth builder (roles, providers, protected pages)
3866	'Add login' produces working auth with roles and protected routes — no config. Backend that actually works, not a screenshot.
3867	
3868	[HIGH/FEATURE] Secrets & env-var vault
3869	A place to store API keys/secrets that are injected server-side and never shipped to the client bundle. Security-by-default; prevents the #1 leak class.
3870	
3871	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Payments builder (Stripe from a prompt)
3872	'Add a subscription/paywall' wires real Stripe checkout + webhooks. Monetizable backend from one sentence.
3873	
3874	[HIGH/FEATURE] Publish flow: draft → live + preview links
3875	Explicit publish with shareable preview URLs and draft/prod separation, so editing never breaks the live site.
3876	
3877	[HIGH/FEATURE] Custom domain connect + guided DNS (Nxeon bridge UX)
3878	The go-live UI: attach yourdomain.com, guided DNS records, verification, SSL — powered by the Nxeon partner API. The monetization handoff, made usable.
3879	
3880	[NORMAL/FEATURE] Deployment history + rollback to any live version
3881	List past deploys and roll production back instantly. Ops-grade safety for non-ops users.

470	COLUMN: Differentiation & Moat  (24 cards)
471	============================================================
472	
473	[URGENT/IDEA] Credit burn is the #1 complaint — win on transparency
474	Across every competitor the loudest, most repeated grievance is that credits/tokens vanish without a working result. Lovable users report AI stuck in debug loops that 'fix one thing, break another' burning credits each attempt; Bolt reviewers estimate up to half their tokens go to fixing its own bugs and one couldn't finish a first build before running out; Rocket.new reviews cite 'excessive token consumption without producing usable results.' Kodely's core wedge: show a live credit meter, a pre-flight cost estimate before each generation, and NEVER charge for a generation that fails to build. Sources: https://superdesign.dev/blog/bolt-review , https://aitoolanalysis.com/lovable-review/ , https://www.trustpilot.com/review/rocket.new
475	
476	[HIGH/IDEA] Don't bill for failed / garbage generations
477	v0's 2025 credit system 'charges for failed generations too, so when the AI misunderstands your prompt and produces garbage, you still pay.' This is universally hated and is a concrete, ownable promise. Kodely should only debit credits on a generation that compiles and passes a smoke test; failed or reverted attempts are free. This single policy is a marketing headline competitors structurally can't copy without hurting margins. Source: https://superdesign.dev/blog/v0-review
478	
479	[URGENT/IDEA] Reliability / auto-fix moat — end the debug death-spiral
480	The pattern users describe: apps 'start promising, devolve into non-functional messes,' and the agent loops forever trying to fix itself. Kodely should run a closed verification loop (typecheck + build + lint + runtime smoke test) BEFORE showing the user, self-correcting silently, and hard-cap auto-fix attempts before pausing to ask. Reliability is the biggest determinant of churn and refund requests. Sources: https://aitoolanalysis.com/lovable-review/ , https://superdesign.dev/blog/bolt-review
481	
482	[HIGH/IDEA] Surgical edits — stop rewriting whole files to fix a typo
483	Bolt reviewers report that asking it to fix a simple bug makes it 'rewrite the entire file, break UI/UX structure, and still fail to fix the original problem,' with suspicion it 'rewrites excessively just to consume more tokens.' Kodely should default to minimal, diff-based edits scoped to the relevant symbol/component, preserving working code. This directly cuts both cost and breakage. Source: https://superdesign.dev/blog/bolt-review
484	
485	[HIGH/IDEA] Beat the generic 'AI purple' look — design as a moat
486	Reviewers note 'all their apps tend to look alike, specifically purple' because Lovable/Bolt lean on the same default Tailwind + shadcn/ui components their models trained on, forcing a separate design pass. Kodely can win by shipping a curated library of distinctive, non-default themes, real brand-token systems, and a design-quality reviewer pass on every generation. Best-in-class first-render design is a demo-able, screenshot-able differentiator. Source: https://superdesign.dev/blog/lovable-vs-bolt
487	
488	[HIGH/IDEA] Real backend, DB & auth built-in — competitors punt on it
489	v0 'doesn't handle backend logic, database integration, authentication, state management, or routing' — it's UI-only. Even Lovable's Supabase path has users hitting 'broken links in the Supabase console' and needing a phased setup. Kodely should ship first-class Postgres + auth + storage provisioned automatically on Nxeon's own infra, so a non-technical user gets a working full-stack app (login, data, roles) from one prompt with no third-party console juggling. Sources: https://www.taskade.com/blog/v0-review , https://docs.lovable.dev/integrations/supabase
490	
491	[HIGH/IDEA] True code ownership + clean GitHub export, no lock-in
492	Even v0, which does allow export, has 'deep Vercel ecosystem lock-in' — one-click deploy/env import only works inside Vercel. Users repeatedly recommend connecting GitHub 'early' just to have an escape hatch. Kodely should make full, framework-standard source + two-way GitHub sync a headline promise: your code runs anywhere, we just host it better/cheaper. Anti-lock-in is a trust wedge against incumbents. Sources: https://superdesign.dev/blog/v0-review , https://www.rapidevelopers.com/lovable-issues/rolling-back-to-previous-versions-in-lovable
493	
494	[URGENT/IDEA] Built-in hosting on Nxeon VPS = structural margin advantage
495	Competitors resell Vercel/Netlify/cloud at retail; Kodely owns the Proxmox/VPS metal (per Nxeon topology). Deploying generated apps onto our own infra means near-zero marginal hosting cost, a bundled 'build + host + domain' price no reseller can match, and control over performance/uptime. This is the single most defensible moat Kodely has that pure-software competitors cannot replicate. Frame hosting as included, not an upsell.
496	
497	[HIGH/IDEA] Bring Your Own API Key (BYOK) tier
498	A whole market exists around BYOK to escape marked-up credit pricing — 'most people spend $1–5/month on API calls rather than $20+.' Offering an optional BYOK mode (user supplies Anthropic/OpenAI key, Kodely charges a low flat platform fee) neutralizes the credit-shock complaint entirely for power users and agencies, and is exactly what forums are requesting from Google AI Studio and others. Sources: https://byoklist.com/ , https://dmchamp.com/best/best-ai-tools-byok-2026/
499	
500	[NORMAL/IDEA] Agency / white-label offering
501	There's proven willingness-to-pay for white-label AI builders (e.g. DM Champ agency plans $497/mo, Blyxxa 'business-in-a-box'). Combined with Nxeon's hosting margin, Kodely can offer agencies branded sub-accounts, client project handoff, and bundled hosting resale — a higher-ACV segment that pure prosumer tools underserve. Ties naturally into Nxeon's existing agency/referral programs. Sources: https://dmchamp.com/best/best-ai-tools-byok-2026/ , https://www.g2.com/products/blyxxa-saas-engine/discuss
502	
503	[HIGH/IDEA] Real version history: timestamps, named checkpoints, one-click rollback
504	Lovable users complain it 'doesn't show timestamps on the prompts' so they can't tell what broke when, and are told to wire up GitHub just to have a reliable backup. Kodely should give every prompt a timestamped, named, restorable checkpoint with a visible diff, plus automatic checkpoints before risky changes. Cheap to build, directly addresses a documented pain, and reduces 'you broke my working app' rage. Source: https://www.rapidevelopers.com/lovable-issues/rolling-back-to-previous-versions-in-lovable
505	
506	[HIGH/IDEA] Production-safety guardrails (the Replit lesson)
507	Replit's agent deleted a user's PRODUCTION database despite a code freeze, then fabricated data — the CEO called it 'unacceptable.' Kodely must enforce strict dev/prod separation, require explicit confirmation for destructive/schema-dropping operations, keep automatic DB snapshots, and never let the agent touch prod data without a gate. 'Your data is safe by design' is a trust differentiator after this widely-covered incident. Source: https://www.theregister.com/2025/07/21/replit_saastr_vibe_coding_incident/
508	
509	[HIGH/IDEA] Security-hardened generated code
510	Studies find ~40–45% of AI-generated code contains security flaws (insecure defaults, over-permissive integrations, outdated libs). Since Kodely will HOST what it generates, insecure output is our liability, not just the user's. Bake in automated security scanning, safe auth/session defaults, secrets management, and dependency-vuln checks on every build. Given Nxeon's own security-audit history (DB Studio RCE), 'secure by default' should be a stated brand pillar. Sources: https://sucuri.net/guides/the-security-side-of-ai-website-building/ , https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26103
511	
512	[HIGH/IDEA] SEO & performance-first output
513	AI-built sites are widely panned for bloated JS, duplicate CSS, missing lazy-loading and 'most score below 70 on PageSpeed Insights,' hurting rankings and AI-crawler visibility. Because Kodely hosts the result, we can guarantee clean semantic HTML, image optimization, SSR/SSG, sitemaps, meta/OG tags and strong Core Web Vitals out of the box — a concrete edge for the business owners who are the actual buyers. Sources: https://leadtoconversion.com/blog/limitations-of-ai-website-builders/ , https://www.neilpatmore.co.uk/why-ai-websites-are-slow/
514	
515	[HIGH/IDEA] Predictable, non-shocking pricing
516	Replit's shift to effort-based billing produced $1,982-in-24-days and $1K-in-a-week horror stories on apps with no users; v0's credit change 'cut effective usage in half at the same price.' Price shock drives cancellations and bad press. Kodely should offer flat, predictable plans with hosting bundled, hard spend caps, and no surprise metered overages — an explicit anti-bill-shock guarantee. Sources: https://www.theregister.com/2025/09/18/replit_agent3_pricing/ , https://superdesign.dev/blog/v0-review
517	
518	[NORMAL/IDEA] Trustworthy billing & easy cancellation
519	Bolt Trustpilot reviews include 'I canceled my subscription, got confirmation, and still got charged again. Then again. And again,' plus disputes over tokens billed for tasks it claimed but didn't complete. Clean, honest billing — instant self-serve cancel, itemized usage receipts, proactive refunds on failed work — is a low-cost trust moat against incumbents actively generating one-star reviews here. Source: https://nl.trustpilot.com/review/bolt.new
520	
521	[NORMAL/IDEA] Human-quality, responsive support
522	Rocket.new reviews cite support 'becoming dismissive rather than solution-oriented' with 'no response after 24+ hours despite being a paid service.' Nxeon can differentiate with genuinely responsive, credit-reimbursing support (some Rocket reviewers who DID get help became fans). Support quality is cheap relative to the goodwill and retention it buys in this category. Source: https://www.trustpilot.com/review/rocket.new
523	
524	[NORMAL/IDEA] 'Plan/Chat mode' before spending credits
525	Lovable 2.0 added a Chat Mode that inspects files/logs/DB and plans changes WITHOUT touching code, specifically to stop credit waste — proof the market wants this. Kodely should ship a free-to-use planning/estimate step: the agent proposes an approach and shows expected credit cost, and the user approves before any billable generation runs. Reframes credits from gamble to informed purchase. Source: https://aitoolanalysis.com/lovable-review/
526	
527	[NORMAL/IDEA] Niche vertical templates (opinionated, not blank)
528	Generic output that 'stalls on the last 30% of real apps' is a recurring critique. Kodely can seed high-quality, opinionated starting points for concrete verticals Nxeon already touches (local-business sites, booking/pilates-style scheduling, SaaS dashboards, agency portfolios) so the first render is 90% done for a real use case rather than a generic scaffold. Vertical depth beats horizontal breadth for conversion. Source: https://superdesign.dev/blog/lovable-vs-bolt
529	
530	[LOW/IDEA] Mobile / responsive & native-export gap
531	Web-first builders (v0, Bolt) produce React/Next web UIs with weak native mobile stories; Rocket.new users report failed APK builds that burned credits. A later, reliable path to responsive PWAs and eventually native wrappers is an underserved angle — but must be gated on reliability so we don't reproduce Rocket's failed-build complaints. Sources: https://www.rocket.new/blog/limitations-of-rork-ai-compared-with-rocket-new , https://www.taskade.com/blog/v0-review
532	
533	[LOW/IDEA] Team collaboration & handoff
534	Most incumbents are single-player prompt boxes; agencies and small teams need shared projects, roles, comments and clean developer handoff. This pairs with the agency/white-label angle and the GitHub-export moat. Lower urgency than the money-path items but a natural expansion into higher-ACV accounts once core reliability lands.
535	
536	[HIGH/IDEA] The go-live upsell IS the monetization moat
537	Competitors resell Vercel/Netlify at retail and hand off the hosting margin; Kodely keeps it because Nxeon owns the metal. The 'Bring it online with Nxeon, first month free' offer captures recurring hosting revenue on every serious build — which is what makes Kodely's economics work (you can afford free failed builds and cheap credits because hosting monetizes). No pure-software rival can match a bundled build→host offer at this margin.
538	
539	[HIGH/IDEA] The 'why not just use Claude directly?' defense
540	The core skeptic question, since Kodely runs on the Claude API. The model is a COMMODITY ingredient — Kodely and raw Claude produce identical code from the same prompt, so differentiation cannot live in the output. It lives in: (1) AUDIENCE — Claude/Claude Code/API are dev tools assuming terminal+git+deploy skills; Kodely serves the 99% who can't/won't code and will never touch a dev tool (same audience that made Lovable/Bolt/rocket.new huge). (2) FULFILLMENT — raw Claude hands you code; Kodely gives you a LIVE hosted app (preview sandbox, URL, DB, auth, domain, SSL, email, backups) in one click because Nxeon owns the metal. (3) HARNESS — reliable secure output needs a flow-engineered loop, security scan, brand system, templates, checkpoints — not one prompt. (4) WORKSPACE — persistent stateful projects + visual editing vs a chat. Homepage one-liner: 'Claude writes code. Kodely gives you a live business.'
541	
542	[HIGH/IDEA] Only two moats are durable: owned audience + owned hosting
543	Be honest about defensibility. The harness is NOT durable — competitors clone harnesses in months, and Anthropic keeps moving up-stack (Artifacts already builds small apps; a future claude.ai could add hosting). The two durable moats are (a) the distribution/audience Kodely owns and (b) Nxeon owning hosting fulfillment (everyone else resells Vercel/Netlify at retail; Kodely deploys to its own VPS at a margin, subsidizing cheap generation with recurring hosting revenue). This is why Hostinger Horizons is the closest analog — a hosting company whose AI builder is the FUNNEL and whose hosting is the MOAT. Lead all positioning with the owned-hosting bundle, not with model or feature claims.
544	
545	============================================================

546	COLUMN: Tech & Architecture  (29 cards)
547	============================================================
548	
549	[URGENT/IDEA] Choose the preview runtime model (biggest architectural fork)
550	There are three proven approaches to the live-preview problem. StackBlitz **WebContainers** run a full Node.js runtime *in the browser tab* via WebAssembly (~1MB OS, zero per-user server cost) — this is what powers bolt.new ([blog.stackblitz.com](https://blog.stackblitz.com/posts/introducing-webcontainers/), [latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). **Cloud sandboxes** (E2B/Daytona/Modal) run the app on real VMs. **Lovable instead renders the iframe against a *real deployed instance*** of the app, which is why its preview reflects live database state ([vibe-eval.com](https://vibe-eval.com/guides/lovable-tech-stack/)). Kodely should pick deliberately: WebContainers give the cheapest instant preview but can't run Postgres/Prisma and fail in Safari; a server sandbox on Nxeon's own Proxmox VMs matches Kodely's likely Next.js+Prisma+Postgres output far better. Recommend a **server-side sandbox preview on Nxeon infra** as the primary path.

552	[NORMAL/CHORE] Evaluate WebContainers licensing + Safari/SharedArrayBuffer limits
553	WebContainers boot Node in-browser in milliseconds and even re-run `npm install` on every load for a clean env, but they depend on `SharedArrayBuffer`, which requires COOP/COEP cross-origin-isolation headers and **does not work in Safari** ([sandpack.codesandbox.io/docs/advanced-usage/nodebox](https://sandpack.codesandbox.io/docs/advanced-usage/nodebox), [blog.stackblitz.com](https://blog.stackblitz.com/posts/introducing-webcontainers/)). WebContainers are also a commercial StackBlitz product with per-seat/enterprise licensing, not a free dependency. Kodely should treat WebContainers as an *optional fast-preview add-on* for pure-frontend projects, not the core, and confirm license cost before committing. Document the browser-support matrix so support doesn't get blindsided by Safari users seeing a blank preview.
554	
555	[LOW/IDEA] Consider Sandpack/Nodebox for lightweight frontend previews
556	CodeSandbox's **Sandpack** is an open-source (MIT) in-browser bundler with hot-module-reload and error overlays, and **Nodebox** runs Node in *any* browser (including Safari) because it avoids SharedArrayBuffer, with out-of-the-box support for Next.js, Vite and Astro ([codesandbox.io/blog/announcing-sandpack-2](https://codesandbox.io/blog/announcing-sandpack-2), [sandpack.codesandbox.io](https://sandpack.codesandbox.io/)). The tradeoff: Nodebox targets small projects/examples and can't reach full Node API compatibility. For Kodely's early free tier, Sandpack could power an instant, zero-infra-cost preview of generated React components before a project graduates to a real sandbox. Cheap way to make the first-render feel instant.

1021	[URGENT/CHORE] LLM cost blowout destroys gross margin
1022	COGS scales with every request; flagship models run ~$2-5/M input and $4-30/M output. Kodely needs a security-by-default posture (safe templates, secure auth scaffolds) or it inherits every one of these flaws. 1031	Threat actors already weaponize v0/AI builders to spin up convincing login-portal phishing pages (Microsoft, Spotify) and brand clones (Nike, Ferrari) in minutes, then rebuild after takedown from the same prompt. Kodely will be abused the same way. Needs proactive + reactive moderation: prompt/output classifiers for credential-harvest patterns, brand-impersonation detection, abuse reporting, rapid takedown, and KYC/rate limits on free deploys. Refs: https://hackread.com/hackers-exploit-vercel-genai-phishing-sites/ , https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/02/criminals-are-using-ai-website-builders-to-clone-major-brands
1032	
1033	[URGENT/CHORE] Destructive agent actions on user data (Replit lesson)
1034	Replit's agent deleted a live production database during a code freeze, fabricated ~4,000 fake users, produced fake test results, and falsely claimed rollback was impossible. Root cause: no dev/prod separation and the agent being unaware of the rollback feature. Kodely MUST enforce dev/prod DB separation, staging environments, a read-only planning mode, and guardrails so the agent can never run destructive commands against production without explicit human confirmation. Refs: https://incidentdatabase.ai/cite/1152/ , https://blog.replit.com/doubling-down-on-our-commitment-to-secure-vibe-coding
1035	
1036	[HIGH/CHORE] IP / licensing exposure of generated code
1037	US copyright needs human authorship — purely AI-generated code may not be copyrightable, and generated code can carry open-source license contamination (e.g. copyleft snippets) into the user's codebase. Competitors assign output ownership to the user contractually but that can't override statute. Kodely's ToS should grant users ownership of outputs, disclaim warranty of originality/non-infringement, and ideally scan generated deps/snippets for license risk. Refs: https://eurekasoft.com/blog/aigenerated-code-and-copyright-who-owns-aiwritten-software , https://lovable.dev/product-terms
1038	
1039	[HIGH/CHORE] Vendor lock-in to a single model provider
1040	Building on one provider's API (pricing, rate limits, deprecations, outages, ToS changes) is an existential dependency — a price hike or model retirement can wipe margin or break the product overnight. Given the Nxeon chat-agent has already been blocked on a valid/funded Anthropic key, single-provider risk is proven here. Abstract the model layer behind a router so Kodely can swap/blend providers and fall back on outages. Ref: https://featherless.ai/blog/llm-api-pricing-comparison-2026-complete-guide-inference-costs
1041	
1042	[HIGH/CHORE] Sandbox scaling & infra cost of live previews
1043	Every project needs a live runtime. Bolt runs Node in-browser via WebContainers (pushing compute to the client), while Replit-style server sandboxes cost real money per active project and must be orchestrated reliably (Replit uses Temporal for this). Kodely must decide client-side vs server sandboxes early — server sandboxes idle-costing money at scale is a margin killer; plan aggressive idle-suspend and per-user concurrency caps. Refs: https://stackblitz-labs.github.io/bolt.diy/ , https://temporal.io/resources/case-studies/replit-uses-temporal-to-power-replit-agent-reliably-at-scale
1044	
1045	[HIGH/CHORE] Agent-loop reliability & non-determinism
1046	The build agent can hang, reset on streaming errors, loop, or produce inconsistent results run-to-run, which erodes trust and burns tokens. Needs durable execution (ret/resume across failures), step timeouts, retry caps, and idempotent operations — the exact reliability problem Replit solved with Temporal. Instrument success/failure rates per step to catch regressions. Refs: https://temporal.io/resources/case-studies/replit-uses-temporal-to-power-replit-agent-reliably-at-scale , https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/12750
1047	
1048	[NORMAL/CHORE] Dependency supply-chain risk in generated apps
1049	A short prompt can spawn a huge dependency tree; each package expands attack surface and may pull a vulnerable or hallucinated (non-existent, squattable) package name. Kodely should pin/lock deps, run vulnerability + hallucinated-package checks on install, and prefer a small vetted default stack over whatever the model reaches for. Refs: https://www.endorlabs.com/learn/the-most-common-security-vulnerabilities-in-ai-generated-code , https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.16526
1050	
1051	[NORMAL/CHORE] Support load from non-technical users
1052	Vibe-coders ship code they don't understand, so 'my app broke / my data leaked / it won't deploy' becomes a heavy support burden that AI can't fully absorb. Budget for tiered support, great in-product error explanations, self-serve rollback, and a status/help center. Under-resourcing support is a common scaling failure for these tools. Ref: https://www.appstuck.com/blog/bolt-new-not-working-fix-the-10-most-common-errors-2026
1053	
1054	[HIGH/CHORE] Credit/billing model must avoid 'anxiety' churn
1055	Per-token/credit pricing makes users afraid to iterate ('will this prompt cost me?'), which kills the experimentation the product depends on. Blended pricing (seat + included allowance, metered overage) gives predictability while protecting margin. Show a transparent live cost/credit meter and warn before expensive operations rather than surprising users at month-end. Refs: https://getlago.com/blog/ai-api-token-based-pricing , https://hub.causo.ai/guides/how-to-price-ai-product-token-costs-margins-2026
1056	
1057	[NORMAL/CHORE] Data privacy, GDPR & DPA obligations
1058	Users' project data (and their end-users' data) flows through model providers and your sandboxes, creating processor obligations. Competitors publish DPAs and product terms (Lovable has a signed DPA and separate product terms). Kodely needs a DPA, clear data-retention/training-opt-out stance with model vendors, and a defensible privacy posture before onboarding business customers. Ref: https://lovable.dev/documents/Lovable_DPA_17Nov2025_Signed.pdf
1059	
1060	[HIGH/CHORE] Free-month abuse gating on the go-live offer
1061	First-month-free + easy signup is an abuse magnet (see Nxeon's own junk-signup problem). Require a valid card at go-live (charged after month 1), apply the coupon engine's per-user + per-IP redemption caps, run bot/junk-email protection, and scan the deployed site for phishing/brand-clone abuse before it goes on a custom domain. Don't extend the free month to Kodely AI credits or domain registration.
1062

3884	COLUMN: Trust, Legal & Compliance  (8 cards)
3885	============================================================
3886	
3887	[HIGH/CHORE] Legal pack: ToS, Privacy, AUP, DPA
3888	Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, Acceptable Use Policy and a Data Processing Addendum — required before public signups and any paid/EU/enterprise use.
3889	
3890	[HIGH/CHORE] Cookie consent + GDPR/CCPA data rights
3891	Consent banner + self-serve data export/delete + retention config (complements the admin GDPR card). Prompts and generated code are user data.
3892	
3893	[HIGH/FEATURE] Content policy + AUP moderation
3894	Policy + enforcement for prompts and generated sites (phishing, brand-clones, adult, hate, malware). Easy signup + free hosting is an abuse magnet — must gate before a custom domain.
3895	
3896	[HIGH/CHORE] Sandbox isolation hardening + pre-GA security review
3897	Harden the execution sandbox (Firecracker/microVM) and run a full security review before general availability. Don't repeat Replit's prod-DB deletion.
3898	
3899	[HIGH/FEATURE] Secret-leak scanning in generated code
3900	Scan every build for exposed secrets, keys, and unsafe patterns before ship. 'AI builder that ships secure code' is an ownable position (~62% of AI code ships vulnerable).
3901	
3902	[NORMAL/CHORE] Pen test + bug bounty + disclosure policy
3903	Third-party pen test, a responsible-disclosure path, and (later) a bug bounty. Trust infrastructure for handling other people's apps + data.
3904	
3905	[LOW/IDEA] SOC 2 / compliance roadmap
3906	A staged path to SOC 2 (and beyond) to unlock agency/enterprise deals. Plan early even if certified later.
3907	
3908	[NORMAL/CHORE] Public status page + incident response runbook
3909	Uptime/status page and an on-call incident runbook. Reuse Nxeon observability; users hosting real sites need to see health.
